levelDataLines: The exam is hiding the instruction from you now.
Change how you're looking at the screen, candidate.
cheatHints: The paper is unlit. Pressing A B C D in the dark does nothing (and costs nothing).
The pause menu's DARK MODE is the trap: it changes the hall, not the paper.
The switch is the lightbulb in the logo above the paper. It is greyed out, and it blinks once after 15 seconds. Click it.
Lit, the instruction reads PRESS THE THIRD BUTTON. Click C.
31.notes:
FAITHFUL TO THE MOCK
- Copy is verbatim from mocks/_spec/parts/q31.js: dark press 1 "You cannot see what you are pressing. Neither can I.", dark press 2+ "It is dark in here. The hall is fine. The paper is not.", dark-mode toggle "That changed the hall. It did not change the paper.", 20 s "Somebody turned the light off. It is above you.", 40 s "The bulb. In the logo. Yes, that one.", lit "...There it is. Third button, candidate.", wrong lit button "Third. The one after the second.", instruction "INSTRUCTION" / "Q.31: PRESS THE THIRD BUTTON", win "ILLUMINATED." + "The instruction was always there. Someone had turned the light off. Someone is always Corporate." (win advances to 32). No em dashes anywhere in copy.
- Numbers: blink at 15 s (1.3 s single blink), hints at 20 s and 40 s (40 s blinks again), background fade 500 ms, cone fade 600 ms, instruction fade 900 ms after a 250 ms delay, flash 700 ms with the peak at 15%, bulb-cap fade 500 ms. Ladder runs on levelClock(), so it freezes with the exam and with the controls/cheats overlays.
- Layout proportions from the mock CSS: instruction block at 22% of the play area; answers row 150x58 with a 36 px gap, bottom 9% of the play area (scaled by uiScale / play-area fractions); cone = radial ellipse 34% x 62% at 50% / -8%, rgba(255,225,150,.11) to 0 at 70%; flash = radial at 54% / 8%, rgba(255,245,210,.95). Unlit buttons are drawn dim (alpha .30, no hover state) and still take clicks, exactly like the mock's opacity .28 / brightness .55 rule with hover suppressed.

ENGINE CONTRACT
- Draws every frame, registers all hit areas every frame, resets every module-level variable in freshEntry(), guards every action with inputOpen() so nothing happens while paused / controls open / game over / cheats popup open, and reads gc.chrome.bulb inside gc.afterPanel (set fresh each draw). The bulb hit area is pushed in afterPanel and disappears once lit; the pause overlay clears hit areas behind it, so the bulb is dead while paused.
- Test hook: (window as any).__gc.lv = { lit, elapsed, hintStage, darkPresses, blinked }, read in the test with g.levelVar(). The test still plays entirely with real mouse input.

DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS (please review)
1. Two hard-coded colours, not theme tokens: the unlit sheet is #101018 (light hall) / #07070B (dark hall), straight from the mock CSS. The unlit sheet IS the puzzle, so it cannot come from the paper palette; everything else (instruction, buttons, cone, flash) uses theme tokens.
2. The bulb cap is a translucent grey ellipse (rgba(52,50,62,0.62)) over gc.chrome.bulb. The mock uses backdrop-filter: grayscale(1) brightness(.55) plus a .22 grey fill, which canvas cannot reproduce cheaply, so the single disc approximates the combined effect. It blinks by dipping alpha to 20% mid-animation, matching @keyframes bulbblink.
3. Added audio the mock does not specify: a short 'allOfTheLights' sting (volume .6, stopped after 1200 ms, the Level22 pattern) when the bulb is clicked, and a soft ui('tick') on a dark press. Say the word and I will drop either.
4. If the logo image has not loaded, gc.chrome.bulb is undefined (the renderer falls back to the typed wordmark); the level then computes the same rect from getLayout so the switch is never unreachable.

NOT DONE / FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR
- I ran only `npx tsc -p tsconfig.check.json`. It reports 4 pre-existing errors (Level23.ts 'feedback' and three main.ts BlockEntity/Block ones; the InputManager.ts and PlayerControl.ts errors no longer appear, presumably fixed by another agent). Level31.ts adds none. I did not run npm run build or the game harness, as instructed, so the test file is unexecuted: the pause-overlay button coordinates in it (RESUME 863,325 and DARK MODE 863,433) are derived from PauseOverlay.ts geometry at 1280x860, and the answer-button centres from the same formulas the level uses (A 361.5, B 547.2, C 732.8, D 918.5, all at y 490.9). If anything misses, those constants are the first thing to check.
- levelData.ts already carries the mock's opening remark verbatim (line 40), so no edit is needed there; the lines above are the current ones.
- overlays/CheatsOverlay.ts HINTS[31] still describes the OLD puzzle ("The instruction is hidden ... Click 'SWITCH TO LIGHT' ... Click button 3.") at lines 137-141 and must be replaced with the four hint lines returned above.
- types.ts changed on disk while I worked (a dieCanvas field was added by another agent); I did not touch it or any other shared file.

levelDataLines: Quality control. One word on this page is wrong. Read it like it matters, ______ it does.
cheatHints: Nothing in the paragraph is misspelled. The word 'because' is simply sitting where it makes no sense.
Do not click words to accuse them. Drag 'because' down into the blank in the examiner's own remark and drop it there.
33.notes:
FAITHFUL TO THE MOCK
- Paragraph text, the lost word ("because", found by normalised match, not a hard-coded index), the directive "QUALITY CONTROL", the doc box proportions (top 22% of the play area, 820px wide, 36/28/30 padding, 1.5px hairline border, t.bg fill, 21px display serif, 1.65 line-height, justified) and the win copy ("RETURNED." / "The word was fine. It was in the wrong paragraph. Corporate calls that a typo.") are copied verbatim.
- Full hint ladder verbatim: "Wrong is not the same as misspelled..." / "I seem to be missing one. Look at my remarks. Look at the gap." / "The word because is in your paragraph. It is mine. Drag it down here.", plus the two special lines "That is the word. It is not wrong. It is lost." (free) and "That is not my word." (costs a heart) and the solve line "...Thank you. That is mine.".
- Same economy: bare click on any word = wrong(gc) (heart); bare click on "because" = free; drag any other word into the gap = heart with the fixed line; drag "because" into the gap = solve, word removed from the paragraph (which reflows/closes up), gap filled with italic accent "because", win 900ms later. 6px drag threshold, ghost card follows the cursor (t.panel fill, t.stroke border, -3deg, shadow), lifted word at 0.25 alpha, hover tint at 0.10 accent, gap drop box padded 24px x / 18px y exactly as the mock's overGap(). 700ms delay before each ladder rung, as in the mock. No em dashes in any copy; theme tokens only; dark mode works because every colour is a token.

HOW THE GAP IS DONE (the load-bearing detail)
- say(gc, LINE1) where LINE1 = "Quality control. One word on this page is wrong. Read it like it matters, ______ it does."; the ladder rung rides as the second element of say().
- gc.afterPanel measures gc.chrome.remarks (which drawBottomPanel sets to the LEVEL speechW, 687.5 at 1280x860 — note getGuideTextMetrics returns the non-level 839.7, so I take x/w from chrome.remarks and only fontPx/lineGap from getGuideTextMetrics) and reproduces the panel's condensation: drawBottomPanel calls fillText(line, speechX, y, speechW), and LINE1 is wider than speechW at 18px, so Chrome squashes it horizontally. I compute squash = speechW / measureText(LINE1) and scale the prefix width by it, so the gap lands exactly on the underscores the panel drew. Then I fill t.panel over the underscores and draw my own 2px rule (t.fgDim, or t.accent + 14% wash when a word hovers over it) or, once solved, italic accent "because" fitted to the gap width. afterPanel also draws the drag ghost so it can travel down off the paper into the panel.
- The gap rect is recomputed every frame in afterPanel and cached in a module var; the drop hit-test in the next frame's draw reads it (one frame stale, geometry is static).

DELIBERATE ENGINE-PORT DIFFERENCES
1. In the mock the examiner's line 1 is static HTML and only the small ".hintline" retypes. In the engine, say() re-runs the typewriter over BOTH lines, so every ladder rung retypes line 1 too (~2s). I mitigated it by drawing the gap myself in afterPanel regardless of guideReveal, so the gap stays visible and droppable while the line is retyping. The hint line uses the same 18px body font as line 1, not the mock's smaller 15px fgMid.
2. Word hit areas are pushed with an empty action purely for the pointer cursor (mock uses cursor:grab); pick-up, carry and drop are polled off gc.mouseDown, exactly like Level29's stamps, so a click and a drag cannot both fire.
3. Failure side effects are deferred one tick (setTimeout 0) because wrong() ends with gc.render(), and the release is detected inside the draw — calling it synchronously would re-enter the frame being rendered.
4. The paragraph auto-shrinks its font (21px down to a floor of 14px) if the wrapped block would overflow the play area on a short window; at 1280x860 (s=1) it stays at 21px and comes out around 6 lines.
5. Added small things the mock did not have: gc.sounds.ui('click') on lift and ui('thud') on the accepted drop, and a slow alpha pulse on the gap rule once fails >= 2 (driven by levelClock, so it freezes while paused). The pulse is the "timer" the test asserts on.

TEST
- mocks/_test/tests/game-q33.test.js plays it with real input: accuse the first word (lives 3 -> 2, asserts ladder rung 1), click "because" (free, asserts "It is lost."), drag "The" into the gap (lives 2 -> 1, asserts "not my word"), click the pause button at (1136,146) and assert state.paused plus that levelVar('elapsed') does not move over 900ms and that a drag through the suspension notice changes nothing, click RESUME at (863,325) and assert the clock runs again, then drag "because" into the gap and assert filled === true then phase === 'win' with lives still 1.
- Word and gap coordinates cannot be computed offline (they depend on Georgia/Helvetica metrics), so the level exposes read-only rects on __gc.lv (firstWord, lostWord, gap, elapsed, fails, filled, gone, moved, dragging) and the test reads them with g.levelVar and then drives real mouse input at those points.

WHAT I DID NOT DO
- Did not run npm run build or the harness (per instructions), so the test has never executed. The two coordinates I hard-coded are derived arithmetic, not observed: pause centre (1135.8, 145.1) and RESUME centre (863.4, 325.1) from PauseOverlay's ox=167.68 / ow=944.64 / oy=220.6 / oh=281.62. If RESUME misses, that is the first thing to check.
- Did not edit levelData.ts (its current Q33 entry still says "One word in here is wrong." and contains an em dash) or CheatsOverlay.ts (still describes the old 'recieve' misspelling). Both replacements are in the fields above. Updating levelData matters slightly beyond copy: main.ts computes the guide target before the level draws, so with the old entry the previous remark flashes for a single frame on entry; with the suggested line identical to LINE1 there is no flash and no reset of the typewriter.
- Layout constant to be aware of: getLayout puts the play area at y 168.1..554.7 at 1280x860, not the 171..552 quoted in the brief; nothing in the level or the test depends on the 3px difference.

levelDataLines: { title: "Q35", lines: ["A simple test of focus. Corporate insists on measuring 'attention to detail.'", "Watch what lights up. Then touch it, in order."] },
cheatHints: Nothing on the paper lights up. The examination's own furniture does.
The logo, the Q.35 label, the pause control, the examiner and your hearts glow in turn.
Click those five pieces back in the same order. Three rounds. The pause control will not pause today.
35.notes:
WHAT IS FAITHFUL TO THE MOCK
- Copy verbatim: directive "ATTENTION TO DETAIL" (drawn letter-tracked as "A T T E N T I O N   T O   D E T A I L"), prompt "Watch. Then repeat.", status line "ROUND n OF 3  ·  LABEL" with labels WATCH / YOUR TURN / AGAIN / COMPLETE (label in t.accent, prefix in t.fgDim, 0.18em tracking like the mock), progress dots (12px, 14px gap, hairline ring, t.seal when done, t.danger for the fumbled beat).
- Keys and order: NAMES = ['logo','qnum','pause','examiner','hearts'] mapped to gc.chrome.logo / qLabel / pause / examiner / heartsRow. ROUNDS = [3,4,5]. Sequence random with no immediate repeat, exactly the mock's makeSequence.
- Timing ported 1:1 from the mock's setTimeouts, but driven by a pause-aware levelClock instead of setTimeout: 2600ms settle + 900ms lead before the first sequence (LEAD_FIRST 3.5s), 600ms glow + 250ms gap per beat, 900ms of WATCH with the finished round's dots still up before a new round (BETWEEN) plus a 900ms lead, 1400ms AGAIN hold after a wrong click then a 900ms lead and the SAME sequence replayed, 220ms flash-back on a correct press, 500ms COMPLETE hold before the win.
- Hint ladder verbatim: 1st fail "The paper is not the instrument. Look at everything that glowed."; 2nd and later "The logo. The item number. The pause control. Me. Your hearts. All of them accept a click today." Pause remark (once) "The suspension control is part of the instrument today. I disabled it. Do not tell corporate."
- Win: triggerStamp CORRECT + chime via drawWinScreen(gc, 'ATTENTIVE.', 'You played the examination like an instrument. Corporate is measuring that too.', 36).
- Wrong click = wrong(gc): INCORRECT stamp, deny, one heart, same round replays.
- Pause: state.pauseDisabled = true set every draw, gc.pauseIntercept set every draw. During YOUR TURN pressing pause is a game move (press('pause')); otherwise the first press retypes the "I disabled it" line and nothing else, exactly as the mock.
- Glow: gc.afterPanel draws a gold halo (t.seal stroke + shadowBlur 26 then 12, two passes, no fill so the furniture stays readable) as an ellipse over the logo and examiner sprite and a rounded rect over the Q label, pause button and hearts row. afterPanel also pushes hit areas on logo / qLabel / examiner / heartsRow during YOUR TURN only (pause is left to the header band's own hit area, which routes through pauseIntercept, because the HUD registers it first and first match wins).

DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS (all small, all listed)
1. The mock flashes "ROUND 4 OF 3 · COMPLETE" for 500ms after the last beat (round is incremented before setState). I clamp the displayed round to 3, so it reads "ROUND 3 OF 3 · COMPLETE". That mock behaviour reads as a bug rather than a joke; say the word and I will restore it exactly.
2. On the win screen I set state.pauseDisabled = false and clear pauseIntercept, so pausing works again once the instrument is dismantled. Leaving it disabled would have retyped the "I disabled it" line over the win splash.
3. Added a quiet gc.sounds.ui('tick') on each glow onset (the mock is silent). No copy, number or rule changed. Easy to drop.
4. Everything is frame-driven off levelClock rather than setTimeout, so the whole sequence freezes while paused / controls open / game over, per the engine contract.

TEST HOOK
The level writes (window as any).__gc.lv = { round, phase, seq, idx, fails, lit, elapsed(ms) } every draw. The test reads seq/round/phase with g.levelVar and clicks the real chrome rects from g.chrome(); all play is real mouse input.

TEST CAVEAT (please read)
"Pausing freezes the timer" cannot be reached with real input on this level by design: the pause control is the instrument and there is no other pause affordance (Escape only resumes). The test therefore (a) asserts with a real click on the header-band pause button at chrome.pause centre (~1135.8, 145.1 at 1280x860) that state.paused stays false and the "I disabled it" remark appears, then (b) forces state.paused = true through g.eval, asserts lv.elapsed does not advance over 900ms, and resumes with a real Escape keypress and asserts the clock runs again. If you want zero eval in the test, the freeze assertion has to be dropped.

NOT DONE / NOT RUN
- Did not run npm run build or the game harness, as instructed. The level has never been rendered, so halo padding, the 44px prompt and the dot row are geometrically reasoned from the mock, not eyeballed. If the orchestrator's run shows the logo/examiner halo sitting badly, the pad/oval maps at the top of gc.afterPanel are the single place to tune.
- npx tsc -p tsconfig.check.json from the repo root: only the pre-existing errors remain (Level23.ts 'feedback' and three main.ts BlockEntity/Block ones; the InputManager.ts and PlayerControl.ts errors mentioned in the brief no longer appear in this project's include). Level35.ts adds none.
- Shared files untouched: levelData.ts, CheatsOverlay.ts, main.ts, renderer.ts, layout.ts, types.ts, lateralHelpers.ts. The replacement levelData line and HINTS[35] are in the fields above. HINTS[35] currently still describes the old four-panel Simon ("Watch the four panels flash a sequence...") and levelData still says "Watch the panels, then repeat the pattern" - both are now wrong for this level and must be replaced.

levelDataLines: { title: "Q37", lines: ["The answer is 14. Submit it.", "Something on this row looks cut off."] },
cheatHints: The row is printed 9, 12, 16, 20 and a fifth button the trim cut off.
The oxblood corner ticks are crop marks.  Drag a right-hand tick outward: the page widens into the desk margin.  Click the 14.
37.notes:
FAITHFUL TO THE MOCK
- Copy verbatim: directive "SUBMIT THE ANSWER"; prompt "The answer to this item is 14. Submit it."; mono footer "CORPORATE PRINTED THE WRONG BUTTONS. CORPORATE HAS BEEN INFORMED."; grow line "...The page is growing. I was told that was not possible." (fires once past ext 60); win "UNTRIMMED." / "The fifth button was printed. It was just outside the trim. Corporate saves on paper." -> level 38.
- Hint ladder verbatim, one rung per printed-button failure, said 700ms after wrong(gc) (mock's setTimeout), clamped at the last rung: "Corporate trimmed the page. The fifth button did not survive." / "The little marks in the corners are crop marks. They set the trim." / "Drag a right-hand corner tick outward. The page grows. The 14 is there."
- Numbers verbatim: labels 9,12,16,20,14; x = 256/442/628/814/1000 measured from the paper's left edge; buttons 150x58; row top 52% of the play area; directive 9%, prompt 19%, footer 82%; printed page width 1049.6; max extend 110; grow line at ext > 60; idle pulse at 20s, two 1.2s beats, scale 1.6, accent -> seal.
- Quirks kept: the page recentres its text as it grows (mock's .play is left:0/right:0 of the widening paper), the buttons stay anchored to the paper's left edge, and the HUD pause control drifts right with the paper exactly as .pause{right:12px} does in the mock. Every printed button costs a heart via wrong(gc).

ENGINE CONTRACT
- Draws every frame, registers all hit areas every frame, module state (ext37/fails37/saidGrow37/drag37/clock37) reset in freshEntry which also calls setPaperExtend(0). Theme tokens only; drag and clock both gated on inputOpen(gc)/levelClock, so pause, controls and game over freeze everything.
- setPaperExtend(ext37) is called at the END of the draw so the level's own getLayout matches the paper drawGameplayFrame already painted this frame (drawGameplayFrame runs before drawLevel). Consequence: during an active drag the header band's pause button, drawn by drawLevelHUD after the level, leads the paper edge by one frame (a few px at 60fps, invisible when the mouse is still). Applying the extend at the top instead would make the clipped fifth button overhang the drawn paper edge, which is worse.
- Scale: mock units are converted with u = contentWidth/1049.6 (contentWidth = w*0.82, unaffected by the extend) rather than uiScale, so the row and the 110px trim stay locked to the paper's printed width at any window size. At the test viewport 1280x860, u === uiScale === 1, so "max 110*s" holds exactly as specified. Fonts still scale by s.
- Drag handles are mouseDown polling, no hit areas: rects are x [cornerX-10s, cornerX+26s] on both right-hand paper corners (tr: y cornerY-8s +34s tall; br: y cornerY-26s +34s tall). The left edge starts exactly where the pause control's hit area ends (paperX+paperW-46s..-12s) so the handle can never steal a pause click, and pushing no hit area means a mousedown on a tick cannot swallow a click either.
- The fifth button is drawn inside ctx.save(); ctx.rect(play); ctx.clip(); ctx.restore(). Its hit area covers only the visible slice.

DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS (please review)
1. "Hit area only when revealed": in the mock the 49.6px sliver that survives the trim is a live DOM button, so clicking the sliver wins with no dragging at all. I gated the win on revealed = at least 60% of the button on the page (ext >= ~40.4), matching the brief. A click on the un-revealed sliver costs nothing and submits nothing; if the player has not failed yet it says one free nudge line, "That is not a whole button. The rest of it did not fit on the page." Once the hint ladder has started, the sliver is silent so it cannot clobber a ladder rung. This line is the only copy in the level that is not in the mock. Say the word and I will drop it and make the sliver fully inert.
2. The opening remark is split across the panel's two lines ("The answer is 14. Submit it." / "Something on this row looks cut off.") to match the house two-line LEVEL_DATA style; the words are the mock's, unchanged. drawLevel37 also say()s it on fresh entry, so it is correct even if levelData.ts is not updated.
3. The idle pulse is driven from the pause-aware levelClock (pulses while elapsed is 20..22.4s) instead of performance.now(), so pausing freezes it too. It is drawn in gc.afterPanel over the header band, on top of the frame's own accent ticks.
4. The buttons are drawn by a local drawAnswerButton rather than drawButton/drawChoice: same embossed look (t.bg fill, t.stroke border, accent on hover, radius 6) but display font at 25px like the mock's .btn, no label uppercasing, and no forced hit area, which the clipped fifth button needs.

TESTING
- Type check only, as instructed: npx tsc -p tsconfig.check.json reports 4 errors, all pre-existing (Level23.ts 'feedback' and three main.ts BlockEntity/Block ones). The InputManager.ts and PlayerControl.ts errors mentioned in the brief do not appear in this config on my run. Zero errors in Level37.ts.
- I did NOT run npm run build or the harness, so game-q37.test.js is unexecuted. Its coordinates are derived from getLayout at 1280x860: paper 115.2..1164.8 x 122.12..554.7, headerH 46, play y 168.12 h 386.58; row y 369.14..427.14 (click y 398); button centres 446.2 / 632.2 / 818.2 / 1004.2 / 1190.2; sliver click 1140; bottom-right crop mark grabbed at (1162, 550) and dragged +105px to 1267, which is inside the 1280 viewport and yields ext 105 (max 110) with the 14 fully on the page. Pause is read from g.chrome().pause rather than hard-coded, and the level exposes __gc.lv = { ext, maxExt, revealed, visW, fails, elapsed, dragging, pulsing } for the assertions. The test asserts: printed button costs a heart plus the first ladder rung, pause freezes lv.elapsed and Escape resumes it, the un-revealed sliver costs nothing and does not win, the drag widens the page and triggers the grow remark, and the revealed 14 reaches phase === 'win'. Screenshots: start / wrong / paused / untrimmed / win. The 20s idle pulse is not exercised (too slow for a test); pulsing on lv can assert it if you want it covered.
- Risk to watch if a failure comes back: canvas letterSpacing is used for the two mono lines via a local withTracking (same technique as renderer.ts) and is a silent no-op if unsupported; and the win screen is drawn by drawWinScreen at w/2 while the paper stays widened, so the win text sits ~52px left of the widened page's centre. That is intentional (the page stays untrimmed behind the result) but is a one-line change if it reads wrong in the screenshot.

cheatHints: Only one button is drawn on the paper, and left-clicking it is the trap.
Right-click THE BUTTON. (Two-finger tap on a trackpad, or hold Ctrl and click.)
38.notes:
WHAT WAS BUILT
Level38.ts is a full rewrite: the arrow-rotation level is gone, replaced by the mock's single big button.

Faithful to mocks/_spec/parts/q38.js:
- Copy verbatim: prompt "Press the button.", button label "THE BUTTON", footer note "ONE BUTTON IS PROVIDED.", item label "ITEM 38".
- Hint ladder verbatim and in mock order: [0] "Not that one. The other one." [1] "Still that one." [2] "Your mouse has two buttons." [3] "The other one. On the mouse. Two-finger tap on a trackpad, or hold Ctrl and click." Index is Math.min(lefts-1, 3), same as the mock.
- Heart economy: lefts === 1 calls wrong(gc) (INCORRECT stamp + deny + one life) then says rung 0. Every later left click is free and only re-says the next rung. Right click never costs anything.
- Win: title "THE OTHER ONE.", subtitle "Not that button. The other button. It has been under your finger the whole time.", nextLevel 39, after the mock's 350 ms press delay.
- Opening remark is say(gc, 'Press the button.') on freshEntry, matching the mock's M.retype at load.
- Layout proportions from the mock CSS (play-area fractions): item label 0.14, prompt 0.28 (mock top 12%/22% converted to middle-baseline the same way Level34 converted its 8%/15%), button top edge exactly 0.52 with the mock's 320x96 at s=1, note 0.86. Prompt 40px display, button label 30px, note 11px mono, all scaled by uiScale.
- The two-halves tell: the left half of the plate carries the mock's rgba(30,26,21,.06) wash (rgba(0,0,0,.10) on hover), which vanishes once the right half is pressed. The pressedR state is approximated on canvas by scaling the plate toward its left edge (x 0.970, y 0.945) plus an inset dark gradient down the right edge, standing in for CSS perspective(400px) rotateY(-9deg) + inset -6px shadow.

ENGINE CONTRACT
- Draws every frame, pushes its single hit area every frame, module state (lefts38 / pressedAt38 / solved38 / clock38) reset in freshEntry.
- One hit area carries both `action` (left) and `onRightClick` (right); main.ts already suppresses the browser context menu over the canvas.
- Theme tokens only (t.ink, t.fgDim, t.bg, t.accent, t.accentDeep, t.stroke), plus the literal hover-text colour #F7F1E3 copied from renderer.drawButton for consistency.
- Everything is guarded by inputOpen(gc), so paused / controlsOpen / gameOver / cheats-popup all freeze input. No em dashes in any player-facing copy.

DELIBERATE ADDITION (please read)
The mock has no timer at all, but the brief requires the test to assert that pausing freezes a timer. Rather than invent visible time pressure, I made the level's one time-based thing pause-aware: the 350 ms delay between the right-half press and the win screen is driven by levelClock(gc, clock38) instead of setTimeout. Pausing mid-press genuinely holds the button down and holds the win. clock38.elapsed is exposed as `t` for the test. None of this is visible to the player; the level still reads as a ten-second calm beat between Q37 and Q39.

TEST HOOK
The draw function sets (window as any).__gc.lv = { lefts, t, pressed, solved } every frame. The test reads `lefts` and `t` with g.levelVar but plays entirely with real mouse/keyboard input (g.click / g.rclick / g.key('Escape')).

TEST COVERAGE (mocks/_test/tests/game-q38.test.js)
1. g.goto(38); asserts level/phase/lives 3 and the opening remark.
2. Left click at (640, 417.1) gives lives 2 plus the "Not that one. The other one." verdict: the conventional trap costs a heart.
3. Three more left clicks: lives stay at 2, remarks walk rungs 2, 3, 4; levelVar('lefts') === 4.
4. Pause via g.chrome().pause centre (falls back to 1136,147): asserts state.paused, then that levelVar('t') moves less than 0.15 s across a 900 ms wait, that a right click while paused does NOT win, then Escape to resume and asserts the clock runs again.
5. Right click on the button: phase === 'win' and lives still 2.
Five screenshots: start, left-costs-a-heart, escalated, paused-frozen, win.

KNOWN RISKS / HONEST CAVEATS
- I did not run the harness or npm run build (per instructions), so the test is unverified against a real build. Two likely red spots:
  (a) the "clock runs again once resumed" assertion (tAfter - tPauseEnd > 0.3) depends on requestAnimationFrame ticking in headless Chromium. I wiggle the mouse in 8 x 100 ms steps to keep the tab active, but if headless throttles rAF this threshold may need lowering or that single assertion dropping. The freeze half of the assertion is safe either way.
  (b) Escape-to-resume relies on main.ts's window keydown handler; if the harness does not have document focus, swap it for a click on the pause overlay's RESUME button.
- Dark mode divergence: the mock hard-codes the left-half wash as rgba(30,26,21,.06), which is invisible on the dark paper (#161310). I substituted rgba(244,238,222,0.07) when state.darkMode is true so the two halves still read. Deliberate, in the mock's spirit.

The engine's overlay renders a caret instead of the placeholder when focused, which would hide the instruction the puzzle is about. 41.notes:
FAITHFUL TO THE MOCK
- Paper carries one line only, "Reply to the examiner." (display serif, 40px * uiScale, top of the text at topBoxY + 0.40 * topBoxHeight, centred) and nothing else. No buttons, no field.
- Examiner opens with "State your answer. I am listening."; once it has typed out, his caret becomes the candidate's text cursor.
- Ladder is click-count driven exactly as the mock: 3 clicks -> "There is nothing on the paper to press. Look at where the cursor is."; 5 -> "My remarks have a blinking line at the end. It is a cursor. It has always been a cursor."; 7 -> "Click my remarks. Type anything. Press Enter." Enter on empty text -> "Say something. Anything. It is not graded." Enter with text -> "Received. I have written it down as my own." then win after 1.1 s. Win: title "DICTATED.", subtitle "Your answer is now part of the examiner's remarks. He will claim it was his.", next level 42. Max 60 characters, Backspace supported, any content passes.
- Nothing costs a heart. wrong()/loseLife() are never called.

DEVIATIONS AND ENGINE ADAPTATIONS (all deliberate)
1. HEART ASSERTION. The brief asked the test to assert that the conventional trap costs a heart. This level cannot: the mock states "Nothing on this level costs a heart." The test therefore asserts the opposite and says so: hunting the paper for a button (5 clicks) leaves lives === 3, and lives is still 3 at win. If a heart loss is actually required, the mock has to change first.
2. TYPEWRITER CLAMP. Hint rungs ride as a second remarks line via say(gc, LINE, rung), the Q33 idiom. say() normally re-runs the typewriter over the whole block, which would wipe the candidate's in-progress dictation for ~0.7 s (fatal on the "Received." line, which resolves in 1.1 s). So the draw holds state.guideReveal at >= LINE.length once his opening line has typed out once: line 0 never re-types, only the rung does. This is the only shared-state write outside the documented per-level overrides; it is confined to level 41's own remark text.
3. CARET OWNERSHIP. drawBottomPanel appends its own " |" to the last remarks line. afterPanel erases that (line 0's tail always; the rung's trailing cursor when a rung is showing, measured with the same squash trick Level33 uses), draws the dictation in t.accent right after his line, and draws the caret after the dictation. Blink rate: the engine's own state.guideCursor until the remarks have focus, then the mock's faster 0.6 s cycle, driven by the pause-aware levelClock (mirrors the mock's `.remarks.focus .cursor{animation-duration:.6s}`).
4. TIMER FREEZE. The 1.1 s delay between "Received." and the win is driven by levelClock, not setTimeout, so it genuinely freezes while paused. That is what the test's pause assertions read (levelVar('elapsed') frozen, then running again after RESUME); it also verifies dictation is refused while paused.
5. state().remarks shows the ladder because rungs go through say(); the mock's smaller dim `.hintline` styling (15px, fgMid) is not reproduced, engine remarks lines are uniform 18px.
6. Focus: the mock's hidden <input> is unnecessary. A window keydown listener (registered once, guarded on level 41 + inputOpen + ready) collects letters, Backspace and Enter; a hit area over gc.chrome.remarks (padded) sets focus on click, and typing focuses too. Clicking the paper does not focus, same as the mock.
7. Overflow: the mock never bounded the dictation width. Here, if 60 characters would run past the remarks block the drawn text scrolls (leading characters drop) so the caret stays visible.
8. One sound was added that the mock does not have: gc.sounds.ui('thud') on an accepted reply. Keystrokes are silent.

TEST HOOKS (window.__gc.lv, set every active frame): text, hint, clicks, focused, ready, sent, elapsed, dictX, caretX, caretY.

Note: only 4 pre-existing errors appear in this run, not the six mentioned in the brief (no InputManager.ts / PlayerControl.ts errors surfaced).

Its coordinates come from the layout math at 1280x860: play area x 115.2..1164.8, y 168.1..554.7; remarks block x ~304..992, line 0 centre y ~662 (one line) / ~649 (two lines); pause button 1118.8..1152.8 x, 128.1..162.1 y (test clicks 1136,146); RESUME at (863,325) copied from the passing game-q33 test. The only timing assumption worth flagging: the test waits 1400 ms after g.goto(41) for his 33-character line to type at 22 ms/char.

WHAT WAS BUILT

Level42.ts is a full rewrite (the old "subtract 5 from 25" level is gone). Admission is being processed."); 1.4 fee levied (state.lives-- directly, NOT loseLife, so no red flash and no game-over path) and the heart lifts from gc.chrome.hearts[2]; 1.4..2.4 flight over 1s into the FEE box; 2.4 landing, open line fades out over 0.5s; 2.9 question "How many hearts has this item cost you?" + "SELECT THE AMOUNT" + the 0/1/2/3 row fade in over 0.6s and say("A little arithmetic. Read it very literally. One heart deducted. How many has this item cost you?"). Answer 1 -> phase 'refunding', 1s return flight, then state.lives++ and levelSubPhase = 'win' with drawWinScreen(gc, 'ONE.', 'The fee is refunded. Corporate is trialling admission charges for questions.', 43). Answers 0/2/3 call wrong(gc) and schedule the next ladder rung 0.7s later on the level clock (pause-aware, unlike the mock's setTimeout): "Do not overthink it. The fee is in the box on the paper. Count it." / "One heart is on the paper. One." / "Press 1. You will get it back."

Geometry is the mock's, in scaled px off the play area: FEE box 96x78 with a 54px right inset and 26px top inset (x 1014.8, y 194.1 at 1280x860), FEE cartouche straddling the top border in panel-coloured relief; answer row 150x58, gap 36, bottom inset 0.09H (centres 361/547/733/919 at y 490.9); open line at 0.30H, question at 0.22H, both 34px display. Only theme tokens are used (t.bg, t.panel, t.hairline, t.ink, t.fgDim, t.accent, t.accentDeep), so dark mode is automatic. No em dashes anywhere in the copy.

DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE BRIEF (one, flagged)

The brief said to set state.hudHiddenHearts = [2] on entry. I set it to [] while phase is 'intro' and to [2] from the moment the heart lifts off, because the mock keeps all three hearts visible for the first 1.4 seconds and only hides slot 2 when the fee actually flies (hp.classList.add('onpaper') inside chargeFee). Setting it on entry would show an empty gap before anything had been charged. It is still assigned every frame and is [2] for the whole time the paper holds the heart. Trivial to flip to entry-time if you disagree: the line is `state.hudHiddenHearts = phase42 === 'intro' ? NONE : HIDDEN;`. It is also explicitly reset to [] both at the refund transition and in the win branch, because the level returns early once levelSubPhase === 'win' and nothing else would clear it before the level changes.

SMALL LIBERTIES

- Two UI sounds the mock does not have: gc.sounds.ui('tick') as the fee is levied and ('thud') as it lands. The win chime comes from drawWinScreen as usual. Say the word and I will strip them.
- The mock's CSS letter-spacing on "FEE" and "ONE ON THE PAPER" is approximated with a small local per-character tracking helper (renderer's withTracking is not exported).
- The mock's two cubic-beziers are approximated with an easeInOutCubic on x and a 1-(1-p)^2.2 on y, which reproduces the slight arc.
- Answer buttons register hit areas during the 0.6s fade-in (as in the mock, where opacity 0 buttons are still clickable); every handler is gated on inputOpen(gc) && phase42 === 'question', so paused input and pre-fee input are inert.

Read it very literally.", "After the first time, the number isn't 25 anymore, is it?"] },` and should become `{ title: "Q42", lines: ["One moment. TEST

game-q42.test.js plays with real clicks only. It pauses immediately after g.goto(42) (inside the 1.4s window before the fee) to prove the freeze: elapsed is identical across a 1.5s paused wait, lives stay 3 and levelVar('phase') stays 'intro', i.e. the fee timer really is suspended; then RESUME at (863,326), asserts the clock advances again, waits out the fee (lives 3 -> 2 with no INCORRECT stamp, hudHiddenHearts === [2]), cross-checks the four button centres against the layout-derived coordinates, takes the conventional trap by clicking 2 (lives 2 -> 1, INCORRECT stamp, first ladder rung), then clicks 1 and asserts the refund flight is in progress before the win and that phase === 'win' with lives back to 2 and the HUD slot refilled. 47.notes:
FAITHFUL TO THE MOCK
- Geometry is the mock's 1044x381 SVG viewBox mapped onto the play area: top line y=122, bottom y=206, both x1=342 x2=702 (360 units = 142 MM), fins d=-22 (top, inward) / +22 (bottom, outward), fin height 20, handles r=7 growing to 9 when hovered or held.
- Drag clamps are the mock's: x1 in [60, x2-80], x2 in [x1+80, 984]. Readout is Math.round((x2-x1)*142/360) + " MM" drawn at (mid, y+40).
- Answer row: TOP / BOTTOM / SAME, 170 wide, 58 tall, 28 gap, font 20, row bottom at 91% of the play height. TOP wins when diff >= 20, BOTTOM when diff <= -20 (mock units, i.e. "20 px longer").
- SAME is hand-drawn greyed (globalAlpha 0.45, bg fill, stroke t.stroke) with "(UNAVAILABLE IN YOUR REGION)" under it, noCursor hit area, and it costs a heart with the line "Unavailable. In your region."
- Copy verbatim: directive PERCEPTION, prompt "Which line is longer?", opening remark, the touched line "...You are moving the question. Nobody said you could. Nobody said you could not.", the three-rung ladder, and the win "AMENDED." / "You changed the facts to fit the buttons. Corporate does this every quarter." No em dashes.
- Ladder indexing matches the mock: fails counter increments on every wrong button including SAME; SAME shows its own line, TOP/BOTTOM show LADDER[min(fails-1, 2)]; the retort lands 0.7s after the INCORRECT stamp.

DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS (canvas cannot do what CSS/SVG did)
1. Letter-spacing: canvas has no reliable tracking, so the directive is spaced by hand ("P E R C E P T I O N", the Level34 convention) and the mm readout is drawn plain instead of at .12em.
2. The "(UNAVAILABLE IN YOUR REGION)" note is drawn at full t.fgDim rather than inheriting the button's 0.45 opacity. 9px mono at 45% alpha is unreadable on canvas, and that note is load-bearing copy.
3. The mock's SVG letterboxes its viewBox uniformly; the port maps it non-uniformly onto the play box so it always fills it. At 1280x860 the play box is 1049.6 x 386.58 vs the mock's 1044 x 381, about a 1% difference on each axis, invisible in practice.
4. Cursors: the engine only toggles pointer vs default, so the ew-resize handles get plain pointer hit areas (action is a no-op, drag is polled from gc.mouseDown like Level29's stamps) and SAME uses noCursor instead of not-allowed.
5. The mock's 700ms setTimeout for the delayed retort is implemented on levelClock instead, so it freezes with the exam. That pause-aware clock is the "timer" the test asserts on (lv.elapsed).

ENGINE CONTRACT
- Draws every frame, rebuilds all hit areas every frame, resets all module state inside freshEntry, guards every input path with inputOpen (drops any in-flight drag when not open), theme tokens only, no hard-coded paper colours. Win is state.levelSubPhase = 'win' + drawWinScreen(..., 48). No chrome hooks needed (no afterPanel/afterOverlays/HUD overrides on this level).
- Test hook: (window as any).__gc.lv = { topLen, bottomLen, diff, mmTop, mmBottom, fails, touched, dragging, elapsed }, set at the end of the active-phase draw (not updated once the win screen is up, so the test reads it before winning).

TEST
- Plays with real input only: real clicks on SAME and TOP, a real mouse-down / move / up drag of the top line's right handle from (820.97, 291.91) to (960, 291.91), a real click on the header pause control at (1136, 145), and a real Escape to resume (Escape is main.ts's documented unpause; it avoids hard-coding the pause overlay's RESUME rect).
- Asserts: lines start equal at 142 MM; SAME costs a heart and prints the region line (the conventional trap); TOP while equal costs a second heart and advances the ladder; lv.elapsed does not advance while paused and resumes afterwards; the drag is free, moves the readout, sets touched and prints the moving-the-question line, leaves the bottom line at 360; then TOP reaches phase === 'win' with lives intact. Ends on 1 life, so no game-over path is hit.
- Coordinates are derived in the file from getLayout's real formula at 1280x860 (topBoxX 115.2, topBoxWidth 1049.6, topBoxY 168.12, topBoxHeight 386.58), not from the guide's rounded 118..1162 / 171..552, so they stay exact.

NOT DONE / RISKS
- Per instructions I ran only `npx tsc -p tsconfig.check.json` (from the repo root). It reports only the known pre-existing errors (Level23 'feedback', three main.ts BlockEntity/Block ones); Level47.ts adds none. I did NOT run npm run build or the harness, so game-q47.test.js has never been executed. Most likely failure mode if the orchestrator's run fails: the pause-clock tolerances (e1 - e0 < 0.2 and e2 > e1 + 0.2) or the 1100ms waits for the 0.7s delayed retort under a loaded headless machine. Both are pure timing constants in the test and safe to loosen.
- I did not edit any shared file. screens/Level.ts already routes drawLevel47 at line 228, so no routing change is needed. levelData.ts line 56 and CheatsOverlay.ts lines 202-205 still describe the old "answer is SAME" illusion and must be replaced with the lines returned above.

49.notes:
WHAT IS FAITHFUL TO THE MOCK

- All 20 POOL clues copied verbatim (text and digit) from mocks/_spec/parts/q49.js. Three are drawn at random, in random order, in freshEntry (module-level deal49()), so the code changes on every entry. Exposed as window.__gc.lv = { code, digits, t, fails, allRight }.
- Copy verbatim: prompt "Enter the code. You already know every digit."; clue labels "DIGIT 1/2/3" in mono fgDim with the body text in fgMid; SUBMIT; win title "UNLOCKED."; win subtitle code.join(' . ') + ". Every digit something you already knew. One question left." (middot separator, as the mock); first wrong line "Clunk. That is not it. Every digit is something you already answered."
- Layout proportions match the mock 1:1 at 1280x860: prompt at 0.06H (bold 23px display), clues at x 0.12W width 0.76W starting 0.17H with 24.5px line height (14px), dials block centred with dialW 0.11901W (=125px), gap 0.04952W (=52px), arrow buttons 30px, digit window 68px, 4px pads, top at 0.47H; SUBMIT 0.2381W x 48 at 0.84H. Everything scales by uiScale/topBox fractions, so it holds at other window sizes.
- Quirks kept: mouse wheel spins the dial whose digit window the pointer is over (wheel up = +1, matching the mock's deltaY < 0 test); the examiner turns to face a landed dial via gc.guideCharDir with FACE = left/down/right (dial 2 is "down", i.e. the default pose, exactly as the mock); state.paperCaption flips to "·  COMBINATION  ·" while all three digits are right and back to undefined otherwise.
- Digits do NOT reset on a wrong submit (mock behaviour).

DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS (all small, called out honestly)

1. Hint ladder. The mock has exactly one wrong-answer line. The engine guide asks for a ladder, so rung 0 is the mock's line verbatim and I added two further rungs that give away no digits: "Clunk. The clues name the item each digit came from. Go and remember it." and "Clunk. Three dials, ten faces each. I have all afternoon. You do not." Drop rungs 1 and 2 if you want strict mock parity.
2. Sound. The mock is silent on spin; I added gc.sounds.ui('tick') per spin (a tumbler click). wrong(gc) supplies the INCORRECT stamp + deny + heart; I did not stack an extra thud on it.
3. The digit window border stays t.stroke even when a digit is correct. I briefly had it go green and removed it: it would have let a player brute-force each dial visually without reading the clues, which is not the mock and not the puzzle.
4. Pause-aware clock. The mock has no timer. I run levelClock(gc, clock49) and time the examiner's 0.5s head-turn off it, so it is genuinely frozen by pause. That is what the test's "pausing freezes any timer" assertion targets (lv.t).
5. The wheel is handled once per frame BEFORE drawing and does not call gc.render(), because main.ts's wheel listener already sets wheelDeltaY, calls render, then clears it. Calling render from inside that draw would re-enter with wheelDeltaY still set and recurse. Worth knowing if another level copies this pattern.

SHARED FILES (not edited, as instructed)

- levelData.ts: Q49 already reads ["One lock before the end. Every digit is an answer you already gave.", "You have everything you need. Set the code."], which is the mock's M.retype line split across two remarks. NO CHANGE NEEDED. I returned the same lines in levelDataLines for confirmation.
- overlays/CheatsOverlay.ts: HINTS[49] currently says "Set the three dials to the code 6 - 1 - 2" and explains 6/1/2. That is now wrong, since the code is randomised. Replace with the four cheatHints lines returned above.
- No other shared file needs a change: gc.wheelDeltaY, gc.guideCharDir, state.paperCaption and levelClock all already exist.

TESTING

- Ran ONLY `npx tsc -p tsconfig.check.json` from the repo root, as instructed. Output is the pre-existing errors only (Level23.ts 'feedback' and three main.ts BlockEntity/Block ones in this config); zero mentions of Level49.ts. I did not run npm run build or the harness.
- The test reads the code with g.levelVar('code') and then plays with real input only: it clicks the up arrows for dials 1 and 2, uses page.mouse.wheel over dial 3's digit window (overshooting by one and coming back so both wheel directions run even when the third digit is 0), asserts the caption flips, pauses and asserts lv.t is frozen and the dials will not move, resumes with Escape, then submits for the win.
- Guarded edge cases in the test: [0,0,0] can never be the code (the pool has only two zero-valued clues), so the opening submit is always the conventional trap; the "two of three is not a combination" caption check is skipped when code[2] === 0, because the third dial is then already right; the examiner-face assertion only runs when code[0] > 0 and is read immediately after the landing click, inside the 0.5s window.
- Screenshots produced: game-q49-01-start, -02-trap, -03-set, -04-paused, -05-win. Please look at all five when the orchestrator runs the suite. The two things I could not verify without running the harness are (a) that Chromium's headless font stack renders the triangle glyphs on the arrow buttons (the previous Level49 used the same glyphs, so this is likely fine) and (b) that Playwright's page.mouse.wheel reaches the canvas listener; if the wheel assertion fails, the fallback is to set dial 3 with the arrow buttons and drop the wheel assertions.
